   - Biologists call it adrenaline (epinephrine). It is released by your adrenal glands when a real or perceived threat appears.  
   - By-products such as norepinephrine (noradrenaline) accompany it; together they raise blood pressure, increase glucose and oxygen to muscles, speed up the heart rate, and shrink “non-essential” systems (digestion, inflammation, pain signals, etc.).
